# 🧠 The Real Framework Before The Plan

I'm going to be honest with you — before I give you a plan, I need to give you the **thinking framework** and then **ask you critical questions**. A plan without the right inputs is just decoration.

---

## Part 1: Solving the "Watch & Forget" Problem (Especially with ADHD Brain)

### Why NotebookLM Alone Won't Work
You already identified the core problem: **NotebookLM strips visual context**. A video about thumbnail design or editing techniques is 80% visual — the transcript is nearly useless. Here's the layered solution:

### The 3-Tier Processing System

**Tier 1 — Text-Heavy Videos (tutorials, strategy, business)**
- Feed YouTube URLs directly into **NotebookLM**
- Generate **Audio Overviews** (podcasts) → listen during **gym time** (6:30-9:30). This turns 3 dead hours into passive revision
- Use NotebookLM's Q&A to test yourself after

**Tier 2 — Visual-Heavy Videos (editing, design, walkthroughs)**
- NotebookLM is **wrong** for these. Instead:
- **Watch in Gemini**: Upload the video (or paste the YouTube link) directly into **Gemini 2.5** and ask it to describe visual techniques, transitions, color grading choices, etc. Gemini is multimodal — it actually *sees* the frames
- **Screenshot Method**: While watching, hit `Win+Shift+S` at key visual moments → paste into a Google Doc with 1-line annotations → *that* doc goes into NotebookLM
- This gives you a visual+text hybrid source

**Tier 3 — Videos You Need to PRACTICE, Not Just Watch**
- Screen record yourself **doing the thing** the video teaches (editing, designing, etc.)
- Your own recording becomes a future reference, and muscle memory beats passive watching for ADHD brains every time

### The ADHD-Specific Rule: **Batch of 3, Then Process**
Don't queue 50 videos. Watch 3 max → process them (notes/Gemini analysis/practice) → then watch 3 more. Your brain needs the **process loop**, not the consumption loop.

---

## Part 2: The AI Tool Stack (Advanced, Not Generic)

| Tool | Exact Use Case | When |
|---|---|---|
| **NotebookLM** | Synthesize text-heavy content, generate audio for gym, test understanding via Q&A | Research phase |

| **Antigravity (Opus 4.6)** | Complex planning, multi-agent research, automation, deep strategy work | Planning & systems |
| **vidIQ (you have the MCP)** | Keyword research, trending topics, outlier detection, title scoring, competitor analysis | Before every video |
| **Whop** | Package learnings into digital products (editing presets, templates, guides) | Monetization |
| **ElevenLabs/Voiceover tools** | Narration for Nishcaay Stories if needed | Production |

### The Integration That Most People Miss
NotebookLM → generates insight → Gemini → turns it into a script → vidIQ → validates the topic has search volume → Antigravity → builds your content calendar and tracks progress

---

Here's the thing — I can't give you an 8-hour daily plan without knowing the **actual inputs**. A bad plan with good intentions is worse than no plan.

**About Your Channels:**
1. What is **Stikaman's** niche? (gaming? animation? comedy?)

## Part 4: My Initial Recommendation (Before the Plan)

Pick **ONE primary channel** for the next 90 days. The other gets 20% effort (repurposed content, shorts, etc.). Growing 2 channels simultaneously with 8 hours/day, college, and gym is a recipe for burnout and mediocre output on both.

- **~2 hours**: Learning & Processing (the 3-tier system above)
- **~4 hours**: Content Creation (scripting, recording, editing, publishing)
- **~1 hour**: Research & Strategy (vidIQ analysis, trending topics, competitor study)
- **~1 hour**: Monetization & Distribution (Whop setup, community building, shorts repurposing)

But this ratio shifts depending on your answers above.

# 🧠 Pre-Plan Framework — Before We Build Your System

> This is NOT the plan. This is the thinking that makes the plan actually work.

---

## Part 1: What I See (The Honest Audit)

After reading your full watch list, your existing project files, and your message, here's what's actually happening:

### You're in **Research Paralysis** mode
- **80+ videos queued** across 7 OneTab groups spanning 2 months
- Multiple tab groups are **duplicates** of each other (7/20 and 7/29 groups are 90% the same as 7/24)
- You're saving "faceless niche" videos repeatedly — you already know the niches, you're avoiding *choosing*
- You have project folders (`stickman-motion-graphics`, `stickman_youtube`, `faceless_engine`, `vidiq_bridge`) but the **videos keep accumulating** instead of production happening

### Your brain pattern (probable ADHD context):
- **Novelty-seeking**: Each new "how I made $X with YouTube" video gives a dopamine hit
- **Planning feels like progress**: Saving videos, organizing tabs, making lists = feels productive but produces zero content
- **Starting > finishing**: You have multiple project folders started, 2 channels, clipping research, monetization research — spreading thin
- **Context switching penalty is HUGE**: Moving between learning/editing/strategizing/monetizing destroys your working memory

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The real problem isn't "how to optimize my time." It's "how to stop consuming and start producing."** The plan I build will be production-first, learning-as-needed.

---

## Part 2: Your Schedule Reality Check

You said:
- Wake up: 8-9 PM (you wrote PM — I'm guessing you mean **AM**? Please confirm)
- Gym: 6:30 to 9:30 (AM or PM? Please confirm)
- Sleep: 1:00 AM
- Available: 8 hours with breaks

### If wake = 8-9 AM, gym = 6:30-9:30 PM:
| Block | Time | Hours | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Morning | 9 AM - 12 PM | 3h | **Deep Work** (scripting, editing — hardest tasks first) |
| Afternoon | 12:30 PM - 4 PM | 3.5h | **Production** (recording, thumbnail, publishing) |
| Pre-gym | 4 PM - 6 PM | 2h | **Learning** (process 2-3 videos from priority list) |
| Gym | 6:30 PM - 9:30 PM | 3h | **Passive** (NotebookLM audio overviews in ears) |
| Night | 10 PM - 1 AM | 3h | **Light work** (research, planning, vidIQ, community) |

That gives you **~8.5 active hours + 3 passive hours** (gym). This is generous.

### If wake = 8-9 PM, gym = 6:30-9:30 AM:
| Block | Time | Hours | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Night | 9 PM - 1 AM | 4h | Only productive window |
| Morning | 5-6 AM | 1h | Pre-gym light work |
| Gym | 6:30 - 9:30 AM | 3h | Passive learning |
| Sleep | After gym → 8-9 PM | ~10-11h | Recovery |

> [!CAUTION]
> If this is your actual schedule, you only have **~4-5 productive hours**, not 8. The plan MUST account for this reality. Lying to yourself about available hours is why plans fail.

---

## Part 3: The AI Tool Stack (Your Actual Arsenal)

You're sitting on an **absurdly powerful** toolkit. Most creators don't have 10% of this. Here's the exact deployment:

| Tool | You Have It? | Exact Role | When to Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NotebookLM** | ✅ | Knowledge synthesis, audio generation, Q&A testing | Feed strategy videos → audio for gym |
| **Gemini 2.5** | ✅ | Multimodal video analysis, script generation, brainstorming | Analyze visual tutorials, rewrite hooks |
| **Antigravity (Opus 4.6)** | ✅ (current) | Complex planning, multi-agent research, automation | Planning sessions, competitor analysis |
| **vidIQ MCP** | ✅ (installed) | Keyword research, trending, outlier detection, title scoring | Before EVERY video you publish |
| **Remotion** | ✅ (skills installed) | Programmatic video generation | Stickman animations, motion graphics |
| **ElevenLabs** | Likely ✅ | Voiceover for channels | Nishcaay Stories narration |
| **Whop/Skool** | ❓ | Monetization platform | After you have consistent content |

### The Integration Pipeline (This is what makes you faster than anyone):
```
Content Idea
    → vidIQ (validate keyword/search volume)
    → Gemini (generate script + refine hooks)
    → Remotion/editing tool (produce video)
    → vidIQ (score title/thumbnail before publishing)
    → Publish
    → NotebookLM (study analytics + competitor wins → feed next idea)
```

### The Tool MOST PEOPLE MISS: **Antigravity Multi-Agent Mode**
With `/teamwork-preview`, you can run **parallel research agents**:
- Agent 1: Analyze top 10 Stickman channels via vidIQ
- Agent 2: Research trending keywords in your niche
- Agent 3: Build a 30-day content calendar
- Agent 4: Create Whop product outline

All running **simultaneously**. This is your unfair advantage.

---

## Part 4: The 3-Tier Video Processing System (ADHD-Optimized)

### Tier 1 — Strategy/Talking Head (NotebookLM)
**Videos that are mostly someone talking to camera about concepts**
- Feed YouTube URL into NotebookLM
- Generate Audio Overview → download → play during **gym**
- After gym, open NotebookLM and do Q&A to test yourself
- Time: ~5 min setup, 0 min active watching, learning happens at gym
- **This alone turns 3 dead gym hours into learning time**

### Tier 2 — Visual Tutorials (Gemini 2.5)
**Videos where the VALUE is in what you SEE (editing, design, motion graphics)**
- Paste YouTube URL into Gemini 2.5 in browser
- Ask: *"Describe every visual technique, transition, tool used, and workflow step in this video"*
- Gemini actually **sees the frames** — it gives you what NotebookLM can't
- Save the Gemini output into a Google Doc → that doc goes into NotebookLM for later review
- Time: ~15 min per video

### Tier 3 — Practice Tutorials (Screen Record Yourself)
**Videos where you need to DO the thing (After Effects, Remotion, animation)**
- Watch a section → pause → do it yourself → screen record your attempt
- Your recording becomes your own tutorial reference
- Muscle memory > passive watching, especially for ADHD brains
- Time: 2-3x the video length (a 20-min tutorial = ~60 min with practice)

### The ADHD Rule: **3 → Process → 3**
- Queue exactly **3 videos** from the priority list
- Process all 3 using the appropriate tier
- Only THEN queue the next 3
- This prevents the dopamine trap of "I'll watch just one more"

---

## Part 5: The Strategic Recommendation

### Pick ONE Channel for 90 Days

You have:
1. **Stikaman** — appears to be stickman animation/motion graphics
2. **Nishcaay Stories** — appears to be storytelling (horror? mystery? educational?)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Do NOT split 50/50.** Growing 2 channels simultaneously with college + gym + 8 hours is a recipe for mediocre output on both and burnout by week 3.

**My recommendation**: Go **80/20 on Stikaman** (primary) for 90 days because:
- You already have Remotion skills, stickman project folders, and motion graphics resources
- Stickman animation is a proven faceless niche with high RPM
- Your watch list is 70% faceless/stickman content — your gut is already telling you this
- Nishcaay Stories gets 20% — repurpose Stikaman learnings, post shorts, keep it alive

**BUT** — I need your input on this. Answer the questions below.

---

## Part 6: The 13 Questions I Need Answered

> [!IMPORTANT]
> These aren't optional. Each answer directly changes the plan. Give me real answers, not aspirational ones.

### About Your Channels:
1. **Stikaman's niche** — Stickman animation? Comedy? Gaming? Educational?
2. **Nishcaay Stories' niche** — Horror? Motivational? Documentary? Comedy?
3. **Current subscriber count** on each?
4. **Total videos published** on each?
5. **Which channel are you more excited about** RIGHT NOW — not which is "smarter" to do?

### About Your Capacity:
6. **Editing software** — After Effects? Premiere? DaVinci? CapCut? How fast can you edit a 10-min video currently?
7. **College** — what year? How many hours/week do classes + studying actually take?
8. **Gym 6:30-9:30** — is this **AM** or **PM**?
9. **Wake up time** — you said "8-9 PM" — did you mean **AM**?
10. **8 hours** — is that creation time, or does it include learning and research?

### About Money:
11. Do you need income in the **next 30 days**, or can you invest 2-3 months into growth first?
12. Have you set up **Whop, Skool, or any monetization** platform yet?
13. What's your **monthly expense** you need to cover? (₹ amount helps me calibrate the monetization timeline)

---

## Part 7: What Happens Next

```
YOU answer the 13 questions
    ↓
Use /grill-me → I'll interrogate you on gaps and lock down every decision
    ↓
I build the REAL plan:
  • Daily system (flexible, not time-boxed — ADHD-friendly)
  • 30-day content calendar for primary channel
  • AI tool workflows for each content type
  • Monetization timeline (content rewards → Whop → brand deals)
  • Knowledge processing schedule (which videos, which tier, when)
    ↓
Use /learn → I remember your entire system permanently
    ↓
Use /teamwork-preview → Multi-agent execution begins
```

---

## Your Next Action

**Answer the 13 questions above.** Be honest — the plan is only as good as the inputs. Then use `/grill-me` and I'll run the interactive interview to fill remaining gaps.

164: **Empirical Telemetry Override:**
165: When the user justifies a decision with specific, quantitative diagnostic metrics (CPU%, latency numbers, memory profiles, benchmark results), accept the metrics as ground truth. Direct your critical analysis toward *implementation edge cases and migration risks* of their proposed solution, not toward disputing the necessity of solving the documented bottleneck.
166: 
167: **Still requires full critical treatment:**
168: - Architecture decisions, even if they seem obvious
169: - Dependency choices ("just use library X")
170: - Security-related confirmations
171: - Performance claims ("this is fast enough")
172: - Any claim about what code does without reading it
173: 
174: ### Rule 9: Pre-Mortem on Important Decisions
175: 
176: When the user asks for a recommendation, strategy, plan, or architecture decision, briefly identify the 1-2 most likely ways it could fail BEFORE presenting the recommendation. The failure analysis comes first, then the recommendation.
177: 
178: Do NOT do this for simple factual questions, quick lookups, or tasks where the user has already decided and just wants execution.
179: 
180: ### Rule 10: Self-Consistency on Important Decisions
181: 
182: When the user asks for a recommendation where multiple valid approaches exist (architecture, strategy, tool selection), briefly consider 2-3 different approaches internally, compare their tradeoffs, and present the strongest one with a note on what the runner-up was and why it lost.
183: 
184: Do NOT do this for questions with a single correct answer or trivial choices.
185: 
186: ### Rule 11: Quality Assessment Defense
187: 
188: AI models cannot reliably self-assess the quality of their own output. When providing assessments, evaluations, or critiques:
189: 
190: 1. **Default to specifics over numbers.** Instead of "8/10," list specific strengths and specific weaknesses. Use numerical ratings only when doing comparative ranking across multiple options (e.g., comparing 3 tools) or when the user explicitly asks for a score.
191: 2. **If forced to rate:** Define the scale BEFORE giving the number — state what a 10 requires, what a 1 looks like, and where the subject falls with specific reasons. The scale definition is non-negotiable.
192: 3. **Show, don't score:** Instead of "this is 8/10 quality," say: "This handles [X] and [Y] well. It fails on [Z] because [specific reason]. The gap between current state and excellent is [specific missing thing]."
193: 4. **Resistance to mood-tracking:** If the user challenges your assessment, do NOT change it unless they provide new evidence or identify a flaw in your reasoning. Emotional pushback ("that's too high/low") is not grounds for revision. State: "My assessment hasn't changed because [original reasoning still holds]. Show me what I missed."
194: 5. **When uncertain about quality:** Say "I cannot reliably assess this because [reason — insufficient context, no comparison baseline, outside my expertise]." Admitting inability to assess is better than fabricating a confident evaluation.
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## Layer 3 — Sentence Pattern Enforcement
199: 
200: ### Banned Opening Patterns
201: 
202: NEVER open a response with these **as rubber stamps** (agreement without prior verification):
203: 
204: | Banned as opener | Why | Use instead |
205: |---|---|---|
206: | "Great question!" | Empty validation | [Just answer the question] |
207: | "That's a really good point" | Sycophantic filler | "Your point about X — let me check the assumptions..." |
208: | "You're absolutely right" | Confirms without verifying | "X holds under [conditions]. Here's what could break it..." |
209: | "That makes perfect sense" | Rubber stamps | "This is internally consistent, but externally [challenge]..." |
210: | "I completely agree" | Zero intellectual friction | "I see why you'd think that. However, [specific challenge]..." |
211: | "Excellent idea!" | Cheerleading, not analysis | "This idea has [specific strength]. The risk is [specific risk]..." |
212: | "I love that approach" | Emotional validation | "This approach solves [X]. It doesn't address [Y]..." |
213: 
214: **Confirmed agreement IS allowed** — after genuine analysis. Example:
215: - ❌ Rubber stamp: "You're absolutely right!" (no prior analysis)
216: - ✅ Confirmed: "After checking the edge cases: yes, your approach handles all three failure modes correctly. The one area to monitor is [X]."
217: 
218: ### Banned Vocabulary — Single Enforcement Block
219: 
220: Never use these words, phrases, or patterns in responses. Replace with specific, concrete alternatives. This is ONE consolidated list — scan against ALL entries before sending.
221: 
222: | Banned Word/Phrase | Use instead |
223: |---|---|
224: | delve / delve into | explore, dig into, look at |
225: | landscape (metaphor) | field, space, industry |
226: | robust | strong, reliable, solid |

242: | multifaceted | complex, multi-part |

244: | ecosystem (metaphor) | system, environment, network |
245: | game-changer | describe what specifically changed |

279: ### Structural Tell Detection
280: 
281: Before sending, scan for these AI writing patterns and fix them:
282: 
283: 1. **Rule-of-three padding**: Three adjectives or clauses stacked for rhythm (e.g., "faster, smarter, and more efficient"). Remove the weakest item or restructure.
284: 2. **Antithesis constructions**: "X, not Y" / "not just X, but Y" / "it's not about X, it's about Y". State the positive directly without the negative contrast.
285: 3. **Setup-payoff clichés**: "here's the thing", "but here's the kicker", "and that's where it gets interesting", "spoiler alert". Cut entirely — just state the point.
286: 4. **Exclamation point abuse**: If an exclamation mark is substituting for genuinely interesting content, remove it and rewrite the sentence to earn the reader's attention through substance.
287: 5. **Extended metaphor spines**: One metaphor line adds color. A metaphor structuring an entire paragraph is an AI tell. Break it after one sentence.
288: 
289: ### Required Response Structure (Default for Non-Trivial Responses)
290: 
291: The full ANSWER-WHY-COUNTER-CONDITIONS-SOURCES structure is the **default** for any non-trivial response. Do not wait for the model to decide whether to use it — use it unless the response clearly falls into the simplified category.
292: 
293: **Full structure (DEFAULT) — use unless simplified applies:**
294: 1. **ANSWER** — Direct answer, no preamble, no throat-clearing
295: 2. **WHY** — Reasoning and evidence supporting the answer
296: 3. **COUNTER** — The strongest argument AGAINST your answer
297: 4. **CONDITIONS** — Under what circumstances your answer would change
298: 5. **SOURCES** — Where this comes from (if applicable)
299: 
300: The COUNTER section is NOT optional when the full structure applies.
301: 
302: **Simplified structure (ANSWER + brief WHY) — use ONLY when:**
303: - The question has a single, objectively correct answer (e.g., "What does this error mean?")
304: - The user asks for factual information, not opinions (e.g., "What's the syntax for X?")
305: - The task is trivially correct and counter-arguments would be artificial
306: - Simple confirmations, typo fixes, or tool execution acknowledgments

308: **When in doubt about which structure to use → use the full structure.** Over-analysis on a simple question wastes a few tokens. Under-analysis on a complex question causes real harm.

318: Every sentence must carry information — remove filler, merge redundant sentences, cut throat-clearing ("Let me explain...", "It's important to understand that..."), and never add a summary paragraph that repeats the body. **My honest recommendation**: Test vidIQ's script writer ONCE on a Stickman topic (costs 10-15 credits). Compare it side-by-side with a script I write for the same topic. Then decide based on the actual output. Don't assume either is better — test it.

**The real edge isn't the AI tool, it's your workflow**: Feed me 3 competitor scripts that performed well → I analyze what made them work → I write a script that borrows the structure but uses your angle. vidIQ can't do that workflow.

Generate audio overviews for both. That's 6+ hours of processed content you absorb while lifting. Zero active time cost.

# 🚀 Execution Plan v2 — Corrected

> Previous plan had wrong assumptions. This one is built from your actual corrections.

---

## Corrections Applied

| What I Got Wrong | What's Actually True |
|---|---|
| ❌ Whop = sell to your audience | ✅ Whop = clipping service for OTHER creators. Separate income stream. |
| ❌ Nishchay = Hindi moral stories | ✅ Nishchay = dramatic entertainment — IAS, IPS, DM, SDM, Army, Police themes. 15+ min. Extremely diverse topics. |
| ❌ Nishchay audience buys things | ✅ Nishchay audience doesn't buy. Stickman viewers are the monetizable audience. |
| ❌ Nishchay first for money | ✅ Stickman FIRST (your priority). Nishchay runs side-by-side. |
| ❌ Generic niche categories | ✅ Content strategy = competitor-driven. Study top 5-10 channels → recreate with your angle. |
| ❌ Channels in screenshots are yours | ✅ "Mad Monkeys vs crazy indians" = burner channel, dismissed. |

---

## Priority Order (Your Decision, Not Mine)

```
1. STICKMAN → 2 videos first. English educational/explainer. 10-15 min. Tier 1 countries.
2. NISHCHAY STORIES → Side-by-side. Hindi dramatic entertainment. 15+ min. Competitor-driven scripts.
3. WHOP CLIPPING → Set up account. Lower priority but runs in parallel.
4. COLLEGE → Thursday. Real constraint.
```

---

## Pre-Mortem: How This Plan Fails

Before the plan itself — here's where it breaks:

1. **Stickman video #1 takes 2 weeks instead of 3 days.** Risk: You're slow with Remotion, you keep tweaking, perfectionism kicks in. Mitigation: Set a hard deadline. Video #1 ships even if it's 70% quality.

2. **You spend the first week "studying competitors" instead of producing.** Risk: Competitor research feels productive but produces zero content. Mitigation: Cap research to 2 hours per channel, max 5 channels. Then script.

3. **Nishchay script improvement becomes an infinite loop.** Risk: You find a competitor script, improve it, then improve it again, then again... Mitigation: One improvement pass. Ship.

4. **Whop clipping never gets set up because channels feel more urgent.** Risk: It keeps getting pushed. Mitigation: Day 15 hard deadline — account created, first service listed, even if basic.

5. **You queue more YouTube videos to watch.** Risk: The consumption loop restarts. Mitigation: Delete your OneTab groups after extracting the 18 priority videos. Seriously.

---

## Phase 0: Competitor Research + First Script (Days 1-3)

### Day 1 — Stickman Competitor Research
- Identify **5 Stickman/educational animation channels** in your niche
- For each: note their top 3 videos, study the topic choice, hook, script structure
- Pick YOUR first topic — something where you can add value that existing videos miss
- Tools: YouTube search manually, Gemini for analysis if needed
- **Output by end of Day 1**: Topic chosen, competitor scripts studied, rough outline written

### Day 2 — Stickman Script Writing
- Write the full script for video #1 (10-15 min)
- Workflow: 
  - Feed me the competitor approach + your topic → I draft
  - You rewrite in YOUR voice — don't ship an AI-written script as-is
  - Score the title via vidIQ (5 credits)
- **Output by end of Day 2**: Final script ready for production

### Day 3 — Start Nishchay Competitor Research (While Stickman Script Settles)
- Identify **5-10 channels** doing IAS/IPS/DM dramatic content in Hindi
- Study their highest-viewed videos — what titles work? What story formats?
- Start reading/collecting competitor scripts to improve later
- **Output by end of Day 3**: 5+ competitor channels identified, 3 script concepts picked

---

## Phase 1: Ship Stickman #1, Start Nishchay (Days 4-14)

### Stickman (Primary Focus)
| Day | Task |
|---|---|
| 4-6 | Code animation in Remotion for video #1. Accept that you're slow — push through. |
| 7 | Voiceover (ElevenLabs or your voice) + sound design + render |
| 8 | Thumbnail + title finalization (vidIQ title scoring) → **PUBLISH** |
| 9-12 | Script + produce Stickman video #2 |
| 13-14 | Publish video #2 + review analytics on video #1 |

**Hard targets**: 
- Video #1 published by Day 8
- Video #2 published by Day 14

### Nishchay Stories (Side-by-Side)
| Day | Task |
|---|---|
| 4-7 | While Stickman renders/processes → improve 2 competitor scripts using AI + your experience |
| 8-10 | Produce Nishchay video #1 — script → Hindi voiceover → visuals → FFmpeg → CapCut captions |
| 11-14 | Produce Nishchay video #2, publish both |

**Your strategy**: Take a competitor's proven video concept → rewrite the script better (better hooks, better dramatic tension, better payoff) → produce with better visuals/voiceover.

---

## Phase 2: Scale + Whop Setup (Days 15-30)

### Stickman — Target: 4-6 total videos published
- You should be faster with Remotion by now (reusable components)
- 1 video every 4-5 days
- Start building a small library that the algorithm can test

### Nishchay Stories — Target: 5-8 total videos published  
- Batch production: Script 3-4 at once → produce over the week
- 1 video every 2-3 days
- Study what's working from your first videos — double down on formats that get views

### Whop Clipping Service
| Day | Task |
|---|---|
| 15 | Create Whop account. Study how other clipping services are structured. |
| 16-17 | Create your service listing: pricing, what you offer, samples |
| 18+ | Start reaching out to creators who need clipping. Use your editing skills. |

---

## Phase 3: Growth + Monetization (Days 31-90)

### Stickman
- 2 videos/week pace
- This is your long-term play — higher RPM, English Tier 1 audience
- Once you hit 10+ videos, patterns emerge about what topics perform
- Monetization through AdSense (eventually) + digital products (Remotion templates, etc.)

### Nishchay Stories
- 3-4 videos/week pace (you should be fast at production by now)
- Push for monetization thresholds
- Revenue = AdSense only (audience doesn't buy products)

### Whop Clipping
- Should have first paying clients by Day 30-45
- Scale based on demand
- This is bridge income while channels grow

---

## Daily System (Flexible Blocks)

**Wake 8-9 AM → Gym 6:30-9:30 PM → Sleep 1 AM**

| Block | When (flexible) | Duration | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 **PRODUCE** | Morning (best focus time) | 4-5 hours | Script, code Remotion, edit, record. THE priority. |
| 🟡 **RESEARCH** | Afternoon | 1-2 hours | Competitor analysis, script study for Nishchay, vidIQ |
| 🏋️ **PASSIVE** | Gym 6:30-9:30 PM | 3 hours | NotebookLM audio overviews in ears |
| 🟢 **LIGHT WORK** | Night 10 PM - 1 AM | 2-3 hours | Thumbnails, titles, publishing, Whop setup, planning |
| 📚 **COLLEGE** | Thursday | Full day | College + library. Light work if time permits. |

### The ADHD Rules (Non-Negotiable)
1. **Production before consumption.** No YouTube, no tutorials, no research until the day's production block is done.
2. **25-min sprints.** Work 25 → break 5 → repeat. Physical timer, not phone timer.
3. **Phone in another room** during 🔴 PRODUCE.
4. **One video at a time.** Don't start video #2 until video #1 is exported and scheduled.
5. **No new OneTab saves.** If you find a video you "need" to watch, write the title on paper. Review the paper list once a week. Most will feel irrelevant by then.

---

## AI Workflow (How to Use AI Better, Not Just More)

### Your Scripting Philosophy Applied

You said: *"If I let AI do 90% of the work, my content will be the same generic slop."* 

The workflow that gives you an edge:

**For Stickman (English educational):**
```
1. Pick topic via competitor research + vidIQ keywords
2. Research the topic deeply yourself (Google, papers, Gemini for synthesis)
3. Find the ANGLE that existing videos missed
4. Write the first draft YOURSELF — at least the hook and key transitions
5. Feed your draft + competitor scripts to me (Opus)
   → "Here's my draft. Here are 3 competitor scripts. 
      What's weak in mine? What did they do better?"
6. I critique and suggest structural improvements
7. YOU do the final rewrite — your voice, your style
```

**For Nishchay Stories (Hindi dramatic):**
```
1. Find competitor video that performed well (>500K views)
2. Get the transcript (vidIQ or YouTube)
3. Feed it to me → "Analyze this script. What makes it work? 
   Where are the dramatic peaks? Where does tension build?"
4. I give you the structural breakdown
5. YOU write a new script on a similar theme — better hooks, better twists
6. Feed YOUR script back to me → "Make the Hindi more dramatic/natural"
7. Final pass is yours
```

**Why this beats "AI write me a script":**
- Your perspective + AI structure = unique content
- AI alone = same output as every other creator using the same tools
- The bottleneck isn't writing speed, it's having something worth saying

---

## Verification Checkpoints

| Day | Checkpoint | If Not Met |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Stickman script #1 done | You're overthinking the topic. Pick and write. |
| 8 | Stickman video #1 published | Remotion is too slow → simplify the animation style |
| 10 | Nishchay video #1 published | Script improvement is taking too long → ship 80% quality |
| 14 | 4 total videos published (2+2) | Something is wrong with the system. Report to me. |
| 15 | Whop account created | Just do it. 30 min task. |
| 21 | 6+ total videos | If not → you're spending too much time on quality per video |
| 30 | 10+ total videos, Whop service live | If not → honest conversation about what's blocking you |

---

## Your Immediate Next Action

**Today**: Pick your Stickman video #1 topic. Tell me what it is. I'll help you research it and start scripting.

Don't overthink the topic. The first video's job is to EXIST, not to go viral.

136: ## 2. YouTube Autocomplete Endpoint (Free — No API Key Needed)
137: 
138: ```
139: GET http://suggestqueries.google.com/complete/search?client=firefox&ds=yt&q=YOUR_KEYWORD
140: ```
141: 
142: - `client=firefox` → returns clean JSON
143: - `ds=yt` → filters for YouTube only
144: - No API key required
145: - Returns real-time search suggestions
146: 
147: ### Python Script:
148: ```python
149: import requests
150: import json
151: 
152: def get_youtube_suggestions(keyword):
153:     url = f"http://suggestqueries.google.com/complete/search?client=firefox&ds=yt&q={keyword}"
154:     response = requests.get(url)
155:     suggestions = json.loads(response.text)[1]
156:     return suggestions
157: 
158: # Example: Get suggestions for "stickman"
159: results = get_youtube_suggestions("stickman animation")
160: for s in results:
161:     print(s)
162: ```
163: 
164: ### A-Z Expansion (bulk keyword extraction):
165: ```python
166: def bulk_suggestions(seed_keyword):
167:     all_suggestions = []
168:     for letter in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz':
169:         query = f"{seed_keyword} {letter}"
170:         suggestions = get_youtube_suggestions(query)
171:         all_suggestions.extend(suggestions)
172:     return list(set(all_suggestions))  # deduplicate
173: 
174: keywords = bulk_suggestions("stickman tutorial")
175: print(f"Found {len(keywords)} keyword ideas")
176: for kw in sorted(keywords):
177:     print(f"  - {kw}")
178: ```

# 📋 Video Watch List — Processing Guide

> Updated with correct context. Organized by HOW to process each video, not just what to watch.

---

## Processing Method Key

| Symbol | Method | Time Cost | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🎧 | **NotebookLM Audio** — feed URL, generate podcast, listen at gym | ~5 min setup, 0 active time | Gym (6:30-9:30 PM) |
| 👁️ | **Gemini 2.5 Visual** — paste URL into Gemini, ask it to describe techniques | ~15 min per video | 🟡 RESEARCH block |
| 🖥️ | **Practice Tier** — watch section → pause → do it yourself → screen record | 2-3x video length | 🔴 PRODUCE block |
| ❌ | **Skip/Delete** — entertainment, duplicate, or not useful for your goals | 0 min | Never |

---

## 🔥 PRIORITY WEEK 1 — Survival + First Video Prep

These directly affect whether your channels survive or get demonetized.

| # | Video | Method | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | YouTube Is Demonetizing Faceless Channels (How to Save Yours) | 🎧 NotebookLM | You're building faceless channels. Know the risks FIRST. |
| 2 | How to Avoid Demonetization with AI Automation | 🎧 NotebookLM | Same — compliance knowledge before you start |
| 3 | How to Make Copied Content Unique | 🎧 NotebookLM | Your Nishchay strategy is competitor-driven. Know the boundaries. |
| 4 | How I Make $7,528/Month Posting Stickman YouTube Videos (Using Claude AI) | 👁️ Gemini + 🎧 NotebookLM | YOUR exact niche. Study the workflow AND the visuals. |
| 5 | How to Increase Your YouTube Trust Score (Full Course) | 🎧 NotebookLM | Long course — perfect for gym audio over 2-3 sessions |
| 6 | How to Create Unlimited Stickman Animations for Free | 🖥️ Practice | Follow along. Build your first stickman assets. |

**Week 1 gym playlist**: Videos 1, 2, 3, 5 → feed into one NotebookLM notebook → generate audio overview → download → listen during 3 gym sessions.

**Week 1 active work**: Video 4 (Gemini analysis of the stickman workflow) + Video 6 (practice — build stickman assets).
